learning_objective: 🎯 Discover why testing and measurement are crucial in sports, learn how to calculate BMI and WHR, and explore standard national fitness test batteries!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Measurement is the quantitative collection of data (e.g., timing a 50m sprint or measuring height). Evaluation is the qualitative judgment of that data against norms or standards to make decisions.
WHR measures fat distribution to assess heart disease risk. It is calculated by dividing waist circumference by hip circumference. Higher ratios indicate abdominal obesity and greater health risks.

Standardized test groups used to measure fitness levels, such as the SAI Khelo India National Fitness Test (measuring speed, strength, flexibility, and endurance across different age groups) and the Harvard Step Test.
Testing helps coaches select talented athletes, classify students into appropriate training groups, monitor progress over time, and identify specific physical weaknesses.

fun_activity.title: 📐 Waist-to-Hip Ratio (WHR) Check
fun_activity.instructions: Using a measuring tape, measure your waist at its narrowest point and your hips at their widest point. Divide your waist measurement by your hip measurement. A ratio below 0.90 for men and 0.85 for women is generally considered low-risk!

exam_tips: 📌 Define Measurement and Evaluation clearly, highlighting that measurement is 'how much' and evaluation is 'how good'.
📌 Know the exact formula and health-risk thresholds for Waist-Hip Ratio (WHR = Waist Circumference / Hip Circumference).
📌 Be able to list the specific test items included in the Khelo India Fitness Test Battery for schools (like the Flamingo Balance Test or 50m sprint).
quick_recap: ⭐ Evaluation without measurement is guesswork; measurement without evaluation is useless data.
⭐ The Harvard Step Test measures cardiovascular endurance and heart rate recovery after strenuous stepping.
⭐ Accurate testing helps athletes prevent overtraining and target specific muscle weaknesses.
